description_full: Allied Gold Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, operates as gold mining company in Africa. It primarily explores gold and silver deposits. The company's flagship project is the Sadiola gold project comprising of 2 mining licenses located in the Republic of Mali. The company was formerly known as Allied Gold Corp Limited & Allied Merger Corporation and changed its name to Allied Gold Corporation in September 2023. Allied Gold Corporation is based in Toronto, Canada.
ceo_bio: Mr. Peter J. Marrone LL.B. | Chairman & CEO | Age 65 | Compensation: $4.1M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 2K people. Revenue per employee of $636K ranks in the below the sector median among Basic Materials peers. Each employee generates $51K of free cash flow annually. CEO compensation is 6× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (10/10).
financial_summary: Allied Gold Corporation is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $3.2B market cap on $1.3B of annual revenue.
Returns on capital run at 161% against a 10% cost of capital — a 151-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 38%.

The business throws off $106M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 155.42× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -24.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 9.9×.

Net dilution runs at 4.2% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 14% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
